parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Prepare for questions from different seats
parts.body:
An executive defense tests whether the plan survives people whose duties differ. The CEO asks why this portfolio advances strategy now. The CFO asks which benefits are observed, when cash is committed, and what happens under low adoption. The CIO asks whether integration and support fit the estate. The CISO asks where data crosses a trust boundary and who can stop an incident. Legal and privacy leaders test intended use and obligations. A business owner asks whether staff can work with the tool. The board asks what management needs it to decide.

Prepare one page of likely questions and point each answer to a line of evidence in the plan. Use a consistent pattern: conclusion, evidence, assumption, decision rule. If a fact is unknown, name the validation step and what investment stays conditional. Do not promise that a future evaluation has already proved a benefit.

Practice disagreement. A CFO may prefer a narrow pilot while the CEO presses for speed. State the reversible step that answers the strategic question without precommitting the full budget. A CISO may reject a vendor data flow; show the alternative and its cost. The goal is sound judgment under conflict, not unanimous agreement.

example.title: A corrected CFO answer
example.body: CFO: 'Your deck claims CAD 1 million in annual savings. Show the arithmetic.' Candidate: 'That claim is wrong. At 40,000 eligible cases, 30% adoption, and six minutes saved per assisted case, the estimate is 12,000 × 6/60 = 1,200 gross hours. At CAD 40 per hour, that is CAD 48,000 of modeled capacity before review effort, vendor and support cost, or setup. There is no measured benefit yet and no cash saving without a documented staffing or redeployment decision. I will retract the CAD 1 million claim, fund only discovery, and return with observed volume, time, correction, and cost.' All figures are illustrative.

exercise.title: Build the challenge sheet
exercise.body: Write two hard questions each from CEO, CFO, CIO, CISO, legal or privacy, and business owner. For each, point to evidence, an open assumption, and a decision that changes if the answer is unfavorable.

sources: OECD AI Principles: accountable roles and risk

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Defend the numbers and thresholds
parts.body:
Show a calculation when challenged. Unit value can be estimated as time saved multiplied by loaded labor cost, minus review, rework, and run cost per eligible case. Then test adoption, case mix, and error severity. A threshold is defensible when you can explain the sample, baseline, affected population, and consequence of failure. '95% accurate' has little meaning without a rubric and error distribution.

A downside scenario should change action. If an assistant saves six minutes on easy claims but adds ten minutes to complex ones, segment the case mix before projecting value. If a subgroup has a materially worse error rate, narrow use or investigate before scale. Do not turn a serious control obligation into a financial trade. Keep the approval authority clear.

Use charts carefully in the defense. Show a sensitivity graph with adoption on one axis and net value on the other, then mark the break-even region. Show quality with sample counts and uncertainty. Exact numbers in your capstone are illustrative until you gather real evidence; label them so the visual cannot be mistaken for measured company performance.

example.title: A full downside challenge
example.body: Fictional plan: 40,000 eligible claims, 30% adoption, six gross minutes saved per assisted case, CAD 40 per usable hour, CAD 1.50 correction and run cost per assisted case, CAD 80,000 annual fixed cost. Gross capacity value is CAD 48,000; variable cost is CAD 18,000; net before fixed cost is CAD 30,000; after fixed cost it is negative CAD 50,000 before setup. If adoption halves to 15% and correction cost doubles to CAD 3, capacity value falls to CAD 24,000, variable cost is CAD 18,000, and the annual result is negative CAD 74,000 before setup. These are scenarios, not realized savings. The CFO refuses scale and authorizes only a bounded test if it can resolve a wider service-quality hypothesis.

exercise.title: Make the case fail
exercise.body: Cut adoption in half and double correction effort. Recalculate annual net value. State whether you continue, narrow, or stop, and what new observation would restore the original recommendation.

sources: OECD due diligence guidance for responsible AI

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Respond when risk changes the plan
parts.body:
Ask a reviewer to inject a plausible event: a vendor changes its model, a customer record appears in an unintended output, an evaluation fails for one language, or an EU rollout adds a new affected group. The candidate should identify immediate containment, incident owner, notification or legal assessment owner, evidence to preserve, and the authority for restart. The exact obligations depend on the facts and jurisdiction; let counsel make that determination.

Separate the first hour from the later decision. Operations may pause a workflow or switch to the manual fallback. Security investigates technical access and logs. Privacy or legal assesses personal-data and reporting questions. The business owner communicates workflow instructions. The CAIO connects the incident to model evaluation and portfolio decisions. Existing incident command and delegated authority take precedence over an invented CAIO override.

Update the plan after the exercise. If model-version change was absent from the test schedule, add a change trigger. If the fallback could not handle volume, revise capacity. Show how an unexpected event changes a control and a funding decision.

example.title: A quality and jurisdiction pause
example.body: In a fictional blind test of 150 English drafts, 132 meet the agreed rubric and 18 need material correction. The team's proposed floor is 93%, while 132/150 is 88%. The claims VP keeps human review and pauses expansion; the evaluation lead checks error severity, case mix, and the rubric, then retests a fresh representative sample. The proposed EU French-language rollout stays out of scope pending its own rights, classification, privacy, and language assessment. English results cannot establish French performance. The floor and figures are illustrative.

exercise.title: Run a twenty-minute incident drill
exercise.body: Have a peer choose one surprise event without warning you. Respond with first action, owners, preserved evidence, stakeholder communication, restart condition, and one roadmap change. Ask the peer where your authority was unclear.

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Keep a critique and revision record
parts.body:
After the mock defense, record each objection, your answer, the evidence that would settle it, and the resulting change. Classify an issue as a corrected error, missing evidence, accepted tradeoff, or disagreement about risk appetite. A response that says 'we will monitor' should identify a measure, owner, frequency, and action threshold before it is closed.

Revise the executive packet itself. If the CFO exposed a false cash-savings assumption, change the financial model and board slide. If privacy counsel identified an uncertain data purpose, move that assessment before pilot data use. If a business owner found no fallback, add the manual path and its cost. Do not hide major revisions in speaker notes.

Run a second defense with the original critic or someone new. The answer need not be perfect. It should reveal what changed, why the chosen option still wins or no longer does, and which uncertainty management has deliberately retained. Preserve the decision log as part of the capstone evidence.

example.title: A defense that changes the decision
example.body: CFO objection: the CAD 1 million savings claim cannot follow from the volume and time assumptions. Revision: retract it; show 1,200 gross hours and CAD 48,000 gross capacity value at 30% adoption, then subtract correction and operating cost. CISO objection: vendor retention is unverified. Revision: prohibit real-data transfer until procurement and security obtain acceptable terms. Quality objection: 132/150 drafts meet the rubric, below the case's 93% floor. Revision: hold expansion, investigate error severity, and retest. The claims VP approves only capped discovery, with a new gate covering net value, data terms, and quality; the board deck and forecast are updated before further funding. This is a fictional defense.

exercise.title: Revise under challenge
exercise.body: Collect at least six objections from two different executive perspectives. Change one portfolio priority, gate, budget assumption, or risk control in response. Explain why any rejected objection did not change the plan.
